title: Unidirectional data flow
caption: State flows down from the repository through the ViewModel to the UI; events flow back up to the ViewModel, which calls the repository's suspending APIs.

edges.label: Flow mapped or shared in ViewModel

title: Configuration, then execution
caption: Configuration evaluates every build script into one task graph. Execution then checks each task's inputs: a cache hit restores outputs instead of running the task, and a miss runs it.

title: Binding across processes
caption: Binding to a service in another process goes through Binder: the activity calls bindService(), the service receives onBind() in its own process, and long work moves to a background thread there.

title: Suspending versus blocking
caption: A coroutine Mutex queues waiting coroutines as suspended continuations and resumes one when the lock is released; a synchronized block instead blocks each waiting thread.

title: Hilt component hierarchy
caption: Hilt's generated components form a hierarchy: each child component can use its parents' bindings, and each one lives as long as the owner it is named after.

title: Bindings in their components
caption: Bindings live in components with matching lifetimes: the database and network client are app-wide singletons, the ViewModel requests the repository, and the activity requests its ViewModel.

title: One change, every consumer
caption: A public change is reviewed against every consumer surface: JVM and KLib ABIs, the generated Swift API, stored schemas and behaviour contracts all feed one versioned release decision.

title: Composition at the platform edge
caption: Each platform's composition root supplies its target bindings, which complete the shared graph; pure domain classes receive dependencies through constructors and never touch the container.

nodes.title: Target bindings
nodes.detail: Context, paths, engines, drivers, native services

title: One common API, one variant per target
caption: A commonMain API needs an implementation for every target: the JVM variant may use java.*, the Apple variant Foundation or POSIX, and the JS or Wasm variant web APIs.

title: Logic-only sharing
caption: Networking, persistence, domain rules and observable state are shared; each platform keeps its own native UI on top of that shared state.

title: Module graph of a KMP project
caption: Build-logic conventions configure the modules; feature modules build on core capabilities, and thin Android and iOS app shells assemble both.

title: From commonMain to two apps
caption: The same commonMain code is compiled by the Kotlin/JVM backend for Android and by Kotlin/Native into a framework that the iOS app uses.

nodes.title: iOS app
nodes.detail: SwiftUI, UIKit, or shared Compose UI

title: Source sets in shared/src
caption: commonMain holds platform-independent code, platform source sets add SDK access, appleMain shares code that iosMain and macosMain inherit, and test source sets sit beside the code they test.
reading: Each boundary is a source set; its cards are the folders or files it contains.

title: What lives in ~/.konan
caption: The ~/.konan directory holds the Kotlin/Native compiler distribution, its downloaded toolchain dependencies and an incremental cache; together they run to gigabytes, which is why CI caches them.

title: Sharing under the new memory model
caption: Threads share a reference freely; the tracing GC marks everything reachable from roots, so the shared User stays allocated while it is reachable.

events.label: Create User and set name to Alice

events.text: User remains allocated because it is reachable

title: Two memory managers in one process
caption: One iOS process runs two memory managers: Swift's ARC frees objects immediately but cannot collect cycles, Kotlin/Native's tracing GC collects cycles in batches, and references across the bridge between them can leak.

title: What commonTest compiles to
caption: commonTest is compiled separately for every target, and each compilation runs on that target's own test runner.

title: Variant-aware resolution
caption: One commonMain dependency declaration resolves to a different artifact for each compilation: an Android/JVM artifact, a device KLIB and a simulator KLIB.

title: Two convention plugins
caption: Convention plugins bundle build policy: company.kmp.library applies the KMP and Android plugins, target and compiler policy and test policy; company.kmp.sqldelight adds SQLDelight and its drivers.

title: From sources to iOS consumers
caption: The Kotlin/Native compiler produces separate device and simulator framework slices; local integration uses them directly, while remote distribution packages them into an XCFramework, a checksummed ZIP and package metadata.

title: Inside an XCFramework
caption: An XCFramework is a bundle of per-platform slices described by its Info.plist; each slice carries its own framework binary, header and modules.

title: Remote SwiftPM distribution
caption: CI uploads an immutable, checksummed archive and tags a Package.swift that points to it; Xcode resolves the tag, downloads the archive and verifies the checksum before choosing a slice.

events.label: Verify checksum and select matching slice

title: The Objective-C bridge
caption: Swift reaches Kotlin through Objective-C: the compiler emits a binary and an Objective-C header, Swift imports that header, and Objective-C's type and naming rules constrain what Swift sees.

title: Shared UI, platform hosts
caption: Shared composables, state and navigation run in every host, while each host still supplies platform seams such as permissions, maps, camera and system UI.

nodes.title: Platform seams
nodes.detail: permissions, maps, camera, system UI, SDKs

title: Diagnose before you fix
caption: Start from the user-visible symptom and collect Compose, platform and dependency evidence before changing code; then fix the measured bottleneck and compare against the baseline.

title: The composeResources directory
caption: composeResources groups resources by type and by qualifier: values-fr and values-fr-rCA localize strings, and drawable-dark supplies dark-theme images.

nodes.title: drawable/
nodes.detail: PNG, JPEG, WebP, BMP, Android XML vectors

title: Resources through the build
caption: Resources pass through the Compose Gradle plugin, which generates the Res accessors and packages per-target resources, into the final application, where release checks confirm locales, themes, missing assets and size.

title: Retrofit's layers
caption: Your code calls an annotated Retrofit interface, a converter serializes bodies, and OkHttp manages the connection pool, interceptors and the TLS socket.

title: Ktor's layers
caption: Your code calls HttpClient, configured plugins wrap each request, and a pluggable engine such as OkHttp, CIO or Darwin owns the TLS socket.

title: From interface call to server
caption: Retrofit turns an annotated call into an OkHttp request, which passes application interceptors, then the HTTP cache, then network interceptors before it reaches the server.

nodes.title: HTTP Cache: Disk entries and validators

title: From crash to readable report
caption: A crash report is persisted on the device when possible and uploaded on a later launch; in the cloud, the build's mapping.txt turns obfuscated stack traces back into readable ones.

edges.label: Uploads if collection and connectivity allow

title: One log call, two destinations
caption: Timber routes one logging call to different trees: a DebugTree writes to logd in debug builds, while a release tree forwards only policy-approved events to crash telemetry.

title: From device signals to dashboards
caption: An APM or RUM SDK collects frame, network and memory signals in the app and uploads them in batches; the vendor stores them as time series behind dashboards and alerts.

title: How an ANR is detected
caption: When the main thread cannot respond before the system's deadline, the system captures process and thread evidence and handles the ANR.

title: What R8 takes in and produces
caption: R8 consumes compiled app classes, library classes and keep rules, and produces shrunk, obfuscated and optimized DEX plus the mapping.txt needed to read stack traces.

title: From benchmark to faster launch
caption: A Macrobenchmark run derives profile rules that ship in the release; at install time the system may compile matching code ahead of time, so measured launch paths do less runtime compilation.

edges.label: Rewritten and packaged by build tooling

title: Making the frame deadline
caption: A frame is smooth only if main-thread and RenderThread/GPU work finish before the display deadline; a missed deadline repeats or delays the frame, which the frame timeline shows.

title: The reference path behind a leak
caption: A leak is a reference path from a GC root to something that should be gone: while the path exists, the destroyed Activity and everything it references stay in memory.

title: One frame through the pipeline
caption: One frame runs from the vsync tick through UI-thread input, animation, layout and draw recording, then RenderThread and the GPU, to SurfaceFlinger composition on the display.

title: Vsync and Choreographer
caption: Each vsync signal starts the main thread's frame work; the display list goes to RenderThread, which hands a rendered buffer to SurfaceFlinger to compose for the next display deadline.

title: The cold-start pipeline
caption: Cold start runs from the icon tap through process fork, class loading, Application and Activity creation and layout to the first visible frame, after which the first network calls and database queries run.
